page.layout: One page of running text, no margin notes. Top: page number and running head. Main text in one column, ending with a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: O' uiua effigies æterni luxq; Parentis, Defendas cœtus optime Christe tuos: Qui tua non ficta discunt oracula mente, Aq; tuo poscunt Numine semper opem.
Decimò, ne illud moleste ferat, quòd hypocritas & mercenarios breui tempore florere, & [illegible, ~12 letters] uidet.

Quid enim? An non Iudex ille mundi suo tempore ad tribunal suum Harmo-stas istos uocabit, & [illegible, ~12 letters] subire coget? Cum Deus eos ad tempus breue Ecclesiam uastantes toleret, tu'ne eos ferre recusabis?

Vndecimò, det operam, ut in eos, qui malam caussam alias male & cyclopicè agunt (cum uidelicet [illegible, ~10 letters] & conuicijs & anathematismis superiores esse contendunt) alias bene seu potius sophistice agunt, intentus, Christi optimam caussam optimè agat, & quoscunque poteft Christo lucrifaciat, uel priuata institutione, uel inculpatæ uitæ exemplo.
Postremò, non solum iudicium posteritatis cordatæ, quod melius erit, præferat stolido præiudicio æmulorum, qui bonos oppugnando inclarescere conantur:

page.notes: Greek words in lines 2 and 3 of the prose, and the Greek word after "uidelicet", are too small and blurred to read letter by letter; marked illegible. Long s rendered as plain s; "ff" in "caussam", "superiores", "sophistice", "subire", "inculpatæ" follows the printed double s. The verse stanza at the top continues from the previous page. The catchword "sed" stands at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. The Greek in the first two prose sentences may be wrongly counted, since the scan is faint.
